definitions.explanation: A person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent. Often used to refer to deceased family members of past generations.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{先祖|せんぞ}⟦{代々|だいだい}→代々：05899_daidai⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}がれてきた→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧。
examples.english: This land has been passed down through generations of ancestors.
examples.notes: 先祖代々 = for generations, from generation to generation

examples.japanese: {先祖|せんぞ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{敬|うやま}う→敬う：00417_uyamau⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: It is important to honor one's ancestors.
During Obon, we welcome the spirits of our ancestors.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{先祖|せんぞ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{江戸|えど}→江戸：19369_edo⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{移|うつ}り→移る：01232_utsuru⟧⟦{住|す}んだ→住む：00673_sumu⟧⟦そうだ→そうだ：10076_souda⟧。
examples.english: Apparently his ancestors moved to this village during the Edo period.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Honoring ancestors ({先祖|せんぞ}⟦{供養|くよう}→供養：11444_kuyou⟧) is an important part of Japanese culture. Key occasions include:
- ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧ (Obon - festival for ancestral spirits)
- ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→お彼岸：08933_ohigan⟧ (equinox periods for grave visits)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先祖|せんぞ}⟦{代々|だいだい}→代々：05899_daidai⟧ (for generations)
- {先祖|せんぞ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{墓|はか}→墓：03549_haka⟧ (ancestors' grave)
- {先祖|せんぞ}⟦{供養|くよう}→供養：11444_kuyou⟧ (memorial services for ancestors)
- {先祖|せんぞ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祀|まつ}る→祭る：03932_matsuru⟧ (to enshrine/honor ancestors)

NEAR-SYNONYM: ⟦{祖先|そせん}→祖先：04047_sosen⟧ is more formal/literary and often used for more distant ancestors or in scientific contexts (human evolution).
